title: Spectral norm of a matrix covered by overlapping rectangular blocks
target: For all complex n-by-m matrices A and finite families of rectangles I_t×J_t covering every coordinate, must the operator 2-norm of A be at most the sum of the operator 2-norms of the restrictions to those rectangles?
decisive_test: Search cross-intersecting incidence families (rows and columns labelled by r-subsets of [2r−1]; rectangle t means both subsets contain t). For test matrices A depending only on intersection size the blocks lie in the Johnson association scheme. Maximize the uniform-vector Rayleigh quotient with each block norm ≤1 via rational linear inequalities in the orbit coefficients. Any strict violation certifies an explicit finite counterexample by exact matrix inequalities; no finite miss can prove the universal claim.
blocker: The original poster identifies cancellation in the existing purported proof. The question is quantum-inspired matrix analysis, not an experimental prediction. May need other rectangle covers or a new norm-decomposition theorem. Ensure witnesses control complex singular values exactly before publication.
attempt: Uniform-vector objective over intersection-invariant matrices, r=2 through 18: exact maximum r, below the required 2r−1. A fresh attempt should address other eigenvectors or asymmetric covers.

title: Rooted closed walks on the middle rail of a three-rail square-lattice strip
target: For every n≥0 count the rooted oriented nearest-neighbor simple closed walks of length 2n with root (0,0) in {−1,0,1}×Z. Empty walk once, no out-and-back of length two. Prove the formal generating-function identity with numerator 1−4x+14x²−24x³+37x⁴−36x⁵+16x⁶−12x⁷ and denominator (1+x²)²(1−2x)².
decisive_test: Generate polygons up to horizontal translation with a 3-tip cut, weight each edge by z, and mark every visited middle-rail vertex w. The derivative at w=1 counts which vertex is translated onto the origin. Multiply nonempty counts by 2 for orientation, add the empty walk, substitute x=z² and verify a rational identity. A022445 (outer rail) should use the same transfer with a different marked rail, not a separate discovery.
blocker: Read Jacques Labelle, Self-avoiding walks and polyominoes in strips (Bull. ICA 23, 1998), and Michael von Thaden’s 2026 three-row polygon enumeration before claims of novelty. The distinction is a specified starting rail rather than unrooted polygons up to translation. Confirm whether a prior paper already supplies the marking.

title: Five-step directed walks constrained by the diagonal
target: Let a(n) count first-quadrant vertex-self-avoiding walks from (0,0) to (n,0) with steps (0,1),(1,0),(1,1),(−1,1),(1,−1). At the departure vertex forbid vertical steps below y=x and horizontal steps above it. For all n≥4 prove a(n)−a(n−1)+(−n²−n+3)a(n−2)+(2−n)a(n−3)+(n−2)(n−3)a(n−4)=0, or give an exact counterexample.
decisive_test: The sum x+y never decreases. On each antidiagonal the walk therefore traverses just one interval, monotonically. Enumerate by entry and exit of that interval using integer arithmetic; derive from this a smaller parity-dependent transition or exhibit the first failure. A short parity recurrence is already posted as code: establish its combinatorial validity before eliminating parity.
blocker: Proving the parity formula depends on a walk-to-recurrence derivation. Existing Maple code implements the counts but gives no derivation in the OEIS entry. Check the author’s related row-refined triangle and literature. Do not count algebraic elimination by itself as a proof from the walk definition.
